_about: The Magic Portals port's movers: the two numbers the Godot project keeps in behaviours.gd
rather than in its data, moved here so they can be retuned without touching code
(Enhanced's own CLAUDE.md rule 1). Both of those are the Godot project's guesses, carried.
`button` is not: it is decoded, and it is read by sim/Puzzle rather than sim/Mover.

_note: RATE_SCALE_K (behaviours.gd:22-26). An oscillating mover - a moving platform, a
patrolling no-portal zone - swings by sin(rate_scale * speed * t) * stride / 2 about
where the level places it. `speed` is a frequency: across the moving_platform
placements speed x stride clusters in a narrow band while each alone varies widely.
The absolute scale is the Godot project's guess; the bytecode constant is not decoded.
speed_px_s's default (behaviours.gd:93, 137). No lift in chapter 1 carries a speed
of its own, so every one of them runs at this.
A pressed button SINKS, and nothing else about it changes: no colour, scale, frame,
sprite, sound or particle (D10's negative result over all 437 instructions of the
four functions). Its `stride` is the node's - 300 in every one of the 46 placements,
and button.ent's own default - so it is not here.
The 6 is in .esc units, and the port takes 1 .esc unit for 1 port unit. INFERRED:
